observations: Photo 0: A silver laptop is open and on top of a stack of identical laptops wrapped in plastic. The screen shows a Windows desktop with a sunset wallpaper. The keyboard is black with a silver touchpad. The HP logo is visible below the screen. A blue Intel Core sticker is on the lower right of the palm rest.
Photo 1: Same setup, but the screen is off. The HP logo is visible below the screen. The keyboard and touchpad are visible. The Intel Core sticker is present. The stack of wrapped laptops is below.

Photo 2: Same as photo 0, but from a slightly different angle. The screen is on, showing the same Windows desktop. The HP logo is visible. The Intel Core sticker is visible. The stack of wrapped laptops is below.
All three photos show the same laptop model, stacked on top of many identical units, suggesting bulk or wholesale listing.
The laptops in the stack are wrapped in plastic, indicating they are new or unused.
The top laptop is powered on in photos 0 and 2, showing a functional screen and operating system.
No visible damage to the top laptop's screen, keyboard, or casing in any photo.
The model name 'EliteBook' is visible on the palm rest in photo 1 and 2, but the full model number (e.g., 840 G8) is not legible in any photo.

The Intel Core sticker is visible in all photos, but it does not specify the generation or exact model. The sticker alone does not confirm 11th Gen.
RAM cannot be verified from photos. No system information or BIOS screen is shown. The seller's claim cannot be confirmed remotely.

The keyboard is visible in all photos, but there is no dark environment or toggle to show backlighting. The seller's claim cannot be confirmed from the images.
No fingerprint scanner is visible on the touchpad or elsewhere in any photo. The seller's claim cannot be confirmed from the images.
